name: Carioca Portuguese
notes: Carioca (Rio de Janeiro city). Coda /S/ is palatal [ʃ ʒ], about 86 % in Brito (2016: 148) (mesmo [ˈmeʒmu], paz [ˈpaʃ]). Strong onset /r/ is a posterior fricative [χ~x]; coda /R/ is velar [x] inside the word and aspirated [h] word-finally (Callou, Moraes & Leite 1998: 62-63). /t d/ affricate before [i] (categorical in Rio in ALiB, Battisti & Dornelles Filho 2015: 226). Callou (2010) is listed but was not consulted for the rule notes.

allophone_rules.notes: The 'chiado carioca': coda /S/ is palatal [ʃ] before a consonant and word-finally (mesmo, paz, dois). Brito (2016: 148): '[ʃ] or [ʒ] account for 85.3% of the occurrences'; the ALiB map gives above 76 % only in Rio de Janeiro, Belém and Florianópolis (Borges & Mendonça 2019: 58, quoting Cardoso et al. 2014: 111). Before a vowel across words it is [z] (Nanini: 17), the sandhi rule RJ_FINAL_SH_PREVOCALIC_VOICE.
Voiced counterpart of RJ_CHIADO_CODA_S: coda /z/ is [ʒ] before a voiced consonant. Brito (2016: 142): 'It occurs as [z] or [ʒ] in syllable-final position followed by voiced consonant' (asma).
Switched off. Vasilévski (2012: 55, Table 1) gives 'xc /s/ exceção' and no opened source gives the value in a spec with a palatal coda, so ⟨xc⟩ keeps [ʃs].
Switched off. A coda ⟨s⟩ of this spec is [ʃ], and coda ⟨x⟩ shares that archiphoneme (Vasilévski 2012: 55, Table 1), so ⟨x⟩ stays [ʃ].

The palatal coda /S/ takes the voicing of a following voiced consonant: mesmo [ˈmeʒmu], desde [ˈdeʒd͡ʒi], Lisboa [liʒˈboɐ]. Brito (2016: 142): 'It occurs as [z] or [ʒ] in syllable-final position followed by voiced consonant' (asma [ˈazma] or [ˈaʒma]). The rule runs in the second pass, after RJ_CHIADO_CODA_S has written the coda as [ʃ]. The list leaves out the tap and reads the next slot on the second pass, after BR_STRONG_R_AFTER_CODA has written ⟨r⟩ as the voiceless strong rhotic [χ], so a coda sibilant before it stays voiceless: desrespeito [deʃχeʃˈpejtu].

Word-final coda /R/. Callou, Moraes & Leite (1998: 62-63): its realisation 'vai de uma vibrante, alveolar ou uvular, a uma fricativa, velar ou glotal, chegando a seu total apagamento'; deletion is 73-82 % in verbs and 32 % in other words (p. 67). The spec writes the aspirate [h].

Non-final coda /R/ (porta, carta) is a posterior fricative, written velar [x] (Callou, Moraes & Leite 1998: 62-63). Barbosa & Albano (2004: 228) give the isogloss: velar and glottal fricatives 'from Rio de Janeiro northwards'. Onset and intervocalic rhotics are untouched.

A coda /S/ takes the voicing of a following voiced consonant: mesmo [ˈmezmu], desde [ˈdezd͡ʒi]. Barbosa & Albano (2004: 229): 'it tends to assimilate the voicing of the following sound'. The list leaves out the tap and reads the next slot on the second pass, after BR_STRONG_R_AFTER_CODA has written ⟨r⟩ as the voiceless strong rhotic [χ], so a coda sibilant before it stays voiceless: desrespeito [deʃχeʃˈpejtu].

An ⟨r⟩ after a coda consonant is the strong rhotic, the posterior fricative of rio [ˈχiu]: honra [ˈõχɐ], genro [ˈʒẽχu]. Cristófaro Silva (2025: 240) puts the R-forte in one class across three contexts: 'início de sílaba que coincide com início de palavra (rapaz, rio, rosa etc.); início de sílaba em meio de palavra (carro, terra) ou início de sílaba após consoante (Israel, desrespeito etc.)'. The Carioca strong /r/ is a posterior fricative (Callou, Moraes & Leite 1998: 62-63).

Switched off. This spec writes every word-final /R/ as the aspirate of RJ_CODA_R_FINAL, which stands after the base rules, so the base drop would pre-empt it in verbs and the base tap list in non-verbs. Callou, Moraes & Leite (1998: 67) give Rio de Janeiro verbs 73-82 % deletion and other words 32 %; the spec keeps one value for both classes.

sandhi_rules.name: final-sh-voicing-before-voiced-consonant
sandhi_rules.notes: A word-final chiado [ʃ] takes the voicing of a voiced consonant at the start of the next word: os dois [uʒ ˈdojʃ], as mesas [aʒ ˈmezɐʃ]. It is BR_FINAL_S_VOICING for the palatal that RJ_CHIADO_CODA_S writes. Nanini (2022: 12), reporting Brito (2016), states the distribution: 'são realizadas como [z] ou [ʒ] em final de sílaba seguidas de uma consoante vozeada'. Her Copacabana count (p. 19, Tabela 1) gives the voiced palatal across a word boundary, '[ʒ] meus neto 159/1033 = 15,39% [‘meuʒ‘nɛ.tʊ]', against '[z] os barros 80/1033 = 7,74% [‘uz ‘bar̄uØ]'. The spec writes [ʒ], the more frequent of the two voiced values and the palatal of the chiado. The strong /r/ of this spec is the voiceless [χ], so ⟨r⟩ at the start of the next word does not voice the sibilant.

sandhi_rules.name: final-sh-before-vowel
sandhi_rules.notes: A word-final /S/ before a word that starts with a vowel is the alveolar [z]: dez anos [ˈdɛz ˈɐ̃nuʃ], os amigos [uz aˈmiɡuʃ]. It is BR_FINAL_S_PREVOCALIC_VOICE for the palatal that RJ_CHIADO_CODA_S writes. Nanini (2022: 17) excludes the resyllabified sibilant from her count because its value is categorical: 'se excluíram das análises os dados de aspiração, apagamento e ressilabificação do /S/ em coda externa, já que a realização deste último nesse contexto é, categoricamente, a fricativa alveolar sonora [z]'. Her example on p. 26 is 'mas era' '[‘mɐi’zɛɾɐ]'.
